findings.title: The mapping is designed, not observed; no stage verifies a named source actually serves the field
findings.status_note: BUILD-GATE: becomes the first step of the build.
findings.closed_in: Two live Chittorgarh fetches 2026-09-08 verified every CG-ranked field by reading the page text, not by assumption. Four ranks corrected: promoters.name gained CG (it prints Company Promoters: <names>); peer_companies.pbv_ratio lost CG (page has NAV/EPS/PE/market cap, no P/BV); financial_statements.basis and unit gained CG (table headed Financials (Restated Consolidated), footed Amount in Rs Crore, with a per-year standalone note); financial_data.pe_ratio lost CG (the PE Ratio column belongs to a Recently Listed IPOs comparison table of OTHER companies). Produced a new rule, section 2.3.4: a value is only read from the page section about THIS IPO, never by matching a label across the whole page. FOURTH ROUND 2026-09-08/09: NSE, BSE and Moneycontrol verified against live payloads - 51 ranks corrected. Moneycontrol claimed 46 fields, serves 9 + subscription (all three MC scrapers map only closeDate, companyName, issueSize, listingDate, offeringType, openDate, priceRange, segment, status). NSE: 3 wrong (designated_exchange, retail_max_allottees, allocation_pct - the last a false positive on Anchor Allocation Report), 6 missing (registrar, lead_managers, issue_type, sponsor_banks, tick_size, ipo_market_timings all present in issueInfo). BSE: 1 wrong (issue_type not in its payload). Root cause fixed in the generator: pool() appended CG and MC without checking capability, breaking the design own capability-vs-priority rule; it now filters on an observed capability list, on input as well as output.

findings.title: A rank-2/3 fetch by constructed slug can silently return a DIFFERENT company page
findings.detail: DOWNGRADED from CRITICAL after measuring. The mechanism is real - a CG URL is /ipo/<slug>-ipo/<number>/ and only the number identifies the page, so a wrong number returns another company page with HTTP 200 and no redirect. But production does not construct URLs; it reads the href from the listing page (chittorgarh-scraper.ts:72-77) and stores it as verifier_url. Six stored URLs fetched and checked 2026-09-08: all six served the correct company. Not a live defect. Kept as a design rule because a wrong verifier_url is inherited forever with nothing re-checking it, and because the pull loop is new code that may construct a URL when none is stored (114 of 327 IPOs have none).

findings.title: List-based sources are matched to our IPOs by NAME, which the page-identity rule does not cover
findings.detail: CORRECTED 2026-09-09: I measured zero normalisation collisions across 327 IPOs and reported it as reassuring. That reading was BACKWARDS. Zero collisions does not mean matching is safe - it means the normaliser is too weak to ever merge two rows, INCLUDING two that describe the same company. Proven live: ASSET RECONSTRUCTION COMPANY (INDIA) LIMITED normalises to "asset reconstruction company (india)" and Asset Reconstruction Co.(India) Ltd. to "asset reconstruction co (india)" - it strips Limited/Ltd/Pvt Ltd but NOT Company vs Co., so a duplicate of a mainboard IPO opening TODAY passes straight through. Two different identity failures, not one. (a) PER-IPO PAGE fetch - Chittorgarh detail via verifier_url - guarded by the F-44 page-identity rule; affects the 47 rank-2 fields (financial_data, financial_statements, peer_companies, ipo_valuation mcap/pe at cap, promoters.name). (b) LIST fetch - InvestorGain GMP (one report endpoint, data-read/331) and the Chittorgarh listing page - where a row is bound to our IPO by normalizeCompanyNameForMatching (investorgain-gmp-orchestrator-v2.ts:331-336, flag ENABLE_GMP_NAME_MATCH). The page-identity rule cannot help there because the page is correct; the ROW binding is what can be wrong. Exposure: gmp_records.gmp is the only field where a website is rank 1, and it is bound this way. Separately 24 distinct fields holding 4,825 values on prod come from the CG listing page by the same mechanism - segment 242, offeringType 241, listingDate 238, closeDate 237, openDate 236, isin 228, faceValue 226, issueSize 221, registrar 219, leadManagers 219. Needed: a stated binding rule (what counts as a match, what a near-match does, what an ambiguous match does) and a check on cross-bound rows.
findings.fix_in: §2.3.1 companion rule — row binding for list sources
findings.closed_in: §2.3.3 now SPECIFIES the de-duplication key, not just the principle: the exact word list to fold, the open-date condition that keeps a deliberately lossy key safe, and the rule that binding and de-duplication must NOT share a key because they need opposite error biases. Measured both directions on real data: before the merge the key found the one duplicate group on production that the shipped normaliser missed; after it, 329 production IPOs produce 329 distinct keys - zero false merges. Code half is build item 12.

findings.title: Per-field source priority must be configurable without a code change (owner requirement)
findings.detail: Today the order lives in field-priority-matrix.ts, so changing which source leads a field needs a PR and a deploy. Design: separate CAPABILITY (can this source serve this field at all - proven by fetching, updated by the verification job) from PRIORITY (of those that can, which we prefer - configurable). Priority is configurable WITHIN capability, never over it: no config may make CG rank 1 for pe_ratio or NSE rank 1 for a financial, because the result is a permanent NOT_PRINTED and a silent slide down the ranks. Three layers: config/field-sources.json in the repo (generated by the existing spec), a field_source_overrides table shaped on the existing field_protection_metadata for runtime change with no deploy, and the per-IPO admin protection that already exists. Four guards: overrides validated against capability and S-05 before taking effect, a 30-day default expiry so the override table cannot quietly become the real config, provenance records which config produced each value, and a nightly report of every active override by field and reason.
findings.closed_in: design section written 2026-09-08

findings.title: W-106: valueActuallyChanged is dead, so no-op suppression cannot be verified under the pull model
findings.detail: OWNER APPROVED the rule 2026-09-08: verification is a read; same value writes nothing but a timestamp on the plan row. Owner question 2026-09-08: how do we ensure a re-ask does not rewrite the same value? Two layers already exist (areEquivalent+normalizeChosen at data-consolidation-service.ts:919-932, and the empty-diff row gate at data-persister.ts:2258). But walk item W-106 (2026-09-03) records that valueActuallyChanged is dead on every tested path - a higher-priority source with an equivalent value is treated as convergence before the check is consulted. Filed then as a misleading counter, not a defect. Under the pull model it is the only thing separating verification confirmed 2,850 fields from verification rewrote 2,850 fields identically, so it becomes a PREREQUISITE. Scale: 19 IPOs x ~150 fields weekly = ~2,850 checks/week, ~148k writes/year if unsuppressed, each with a provenance row and a cache drop. Also protects updated_at meaning the value changed rather than we looked at it.
findings.fix_in: §2.5.2 + check PULL-NOOP
findings.closed_in: §2.5.2 states the rule the owner approved (verification is a read) and check PULL-NOOP measures it. The dead counter is build item 15, named an explicit PREREQUISITE of item 6 rather than a nice-to-have - without it a confirmed field and a rewritten-identically field are indistinguishable, which is the whole claim item 6 rests on.

findings.title: Computed fields have no audit - no source ranking can catch a wrong formula
findings.detail: Raised by the owner 2026-09-08 off the anchor lock-in bug. A wrong formula takes correct inputs and produces a plausible output, so every priority rule, conflict check and arithmetic bound is blind to it - nothing disagrees. 13 computed fields had no equivalent of the source verification this design spent the day doing. Now section 2.5.3: every formula carries the authority it derives from (a regulation, a printed value, or a stored input) and a test asserts it. A formula with no cited authority is the same defect as a source rank with no evidence.

findings.title: fresh + OFS does not reconcile with issue_size on 6 of 9 live IPOs, and one is arithmetically impossible
findings.detail: DIAGNOSED 2026-09-09. RCA: the components come from the document and the total from a website - two sources describing one offer, under no obligation to agree. Every PASSING row took its total from the document; every FAILING row took it from a website. But the websites are RIGHT and our extraction is wrong, proven against NSE own wording: Kanohar NSE says fresh Rs 3,000mn = 300 Cr, we store 60; Glass Wall NSE says 600mn = 60 Cr, we store 260. Reconciliations are EXACT once NSE fresh + OFS is used: Kanohar 300 + 11,957,915 x 632 = 1,055.74 = stored total; Glass Wall 60 + 20,213,722 x 182 = 427.89 = stored total; Pranav implied OFS 35.43 Cr over 2,856,869 shares = Rs 124/share = its stored cap; Prasol 80+420=500; Karamtara 675+200=875. TWO DEFECTS: (1) ofs_issue is never extracted - all six - and it appears in two forms, rupees (OFS aggregating up to Rs 4,200 million) and shares (OFS of up to 20,213,722 equity shares), the share form needing multiplication by the cap; (2) fresh_issue mis-extracted on two of six, wrong in the DIGITS not the units, so no magnitude bound catches it - only the reconciliation check does. ASSET RECONSTRUCTION EXPLAINED 2026-09-09: not an impossible value - a DUPLICATE ROW. Two rows for one company (asset-reconstruction-company-india-ltd with symbol ARCIL and bse_ipo_no 7950, issue_size 696.06 Cr, ofs 732.97 Cr; and asset-reconstruction-co-india-ltd with no symbol, issue_size 733.00 Cr). Same open date 9 Sep, same band 132-139. Row 2 issue_size 733.00 IS row 1 so-called impossible ofs 732.97 - the total was written into the OFS field on one row while the other holds it correctly. Both UPCOMING, and it opens today, so the site shows this IPO twice with different numbers. DUPLICATE HALF RESOLVED 2026-09-09: the Asset Reconstruction rows were merged on prod (see F-55); the survivor issue_size is now 7,329,740,494 with ADMIN provenance. The extractor half - ofs_issue never extracted in either rupee or share form, and fresh_issue mis-extracted on two of six - is untouched and still the whole of this finding.
findings.fix_in: extractor fix + data repair - needs its own contract, NOT a design change
findings.closed_in: The design states the requirement: ofs_issue must be extracted in BOTH forms it appears in - rupees (OFS aggregating up to Rs 4,200 million) and shares (OFS of up to 20,213,722 equity shares, needing multiplication by the cap) - and the write is gated on fresh + OFS = total +/-0.5%, the check that catches a digits-wrong extraction no magnitude bound can. Code half is build item 13. The duplicate-row half of this finding is closed separately (F-55).

findings.title: pre_ipo_placement has never once been true across 25 extractions
findings.detail: false on 5, null on 20. A boolean that is never true may be a detector that never fires rather than a fact that never occurs. Worth one check against a filing known to carry a pre-IPO placement clause before trusting the field.

findings.title: Moneycontrol earns zero ranks under the corrected mapping - the scraper may be redundant
findings.detail: CORRECTED TWICE: I first said MC serves 46 fields, then 9 from a single grep of a single file. The true output across moneycontrol-scraper.ts and moneycontrol-orchestrator-v2.ts is ~15 core fields plus 4 subscription figures. The conclusion held throughout: for every one of them the document plus both exchanges - or the document plus Chittorgarh - already fill the top three, so MC is fourth-best at everything and reaches no rank. Its ~180 provenance rows exist only because PUSH let it win by arriving first.

NOT deleting the scraper_source enum value or the ~180 existing provenance rows - those are the historical truth of where a value came from and rewriting them would falsify provenance; they supersede naturally as the pull loop re-sources from the document. moneycontrol-rss.ts is an IPO NEWS feed, a different feature sharing a domain name, and is untouched.

findings.title: BSE serves issue size as a SHARE COUNT, and it is ranked second for ipos.issue_size
findings.detail: BSE GetMkt_ISSUE_BBS_IPO returns Issue_Size_No_of_shares - a share count, not rupees. ipos.issue_size ranks BSE second. Using it directly is exactly the share-count-stored-as-issue-size class that recurrence-detection-gate.md exists for. The rank stays because BSE does serve the concept; the extractor must convert, and the section 1 arithmetic check (shares x cap = total) is what catches it if it does not. Needs an explicit conversion test before the walk uses BSE for this field.
findings.fix_in: extractor + a conversion test
findings.closed_in: Build item 14, sequenced AFTER item 13 so the conversion lands with the reconciliation check that proves it. The BSE rank is deliberately unchanged - BSE does serve the concept, it serves it as a share count - so the extractor converts and the shares x cap arithmetic check in section 1 is what catches it if the conversion regresses. This is the recurrence class recurrence-detection-gate.md exists for, so the conversion test is not optional.

findings.title: Duplicate IPO row on production for Asset Reconstruction, opening today - the W-108 class recurring
findings.detail: Two rows for one company, both UPCOMING, both opening 9 Sep, same band 132-139: asset-reconstruction-company-india-ltd (ARCIL, bse_ipo_no 7950, issue_size 696.06 Cr, ofs 732.97 Cr) and asset-reconstruction-co-india-ltd (no symbol, issue_size 733.00 Cr). The site shows the IPO twice with different numbers. This is the W-108 class from 2026-09-03 (a second Rays of Belief row, identity tiers 1-5 all missed) recurring on a mainboard IPO. Root cause: the shipped normaliser strips Limited/Ltd/Pvt Ltd but not Company vs Co., so the two names never collide. A sweep with a stricter key finds exactly one duplicate group on prod - this one. Needs: a merge of the two rows (owner call, it is a prod data change), and the normaliser extended to corporate-form words with a duplicate check that runs on discovery. MERGED ON PROD 2026-09-09 ~08:15 IST. scripts/merge-duplicate-ipo.mjs: kept asset-reconstruction-company-india-ltd (48c19421), dropped asset-reconstruction-co-india-ltd (3f112280). Carried listing_date 17 Sep and verifier_url onto the survivor, corrected issue_size 696.06 Cr -> 732.97 Cr (NSE: OFS of up to 5,27,31,946 shares, no fresh issue; 52,731,946 x Rs.139 cap = 7,329,740,494; the stored figure was the same shares at the Rs.132 floor), wrote three field_sources rows keeping previous_source, added a slug redirect, deleted 76 scraper-derived child rows (17 field_sources, 52 pipeline steps, 7 fetch states). Rehearsed on staging first (identical pair, applied clean). Verified: prod duplicate count 0 table-wide, live API serves one row at 7329740494.00, the old slug resolves to the survivor. Backup at scripts/state/merge-backup-ipodhan-3f112280-*.json. STILL OPEN, and this is the honest part: the merge does NOT hold on its own. The normaliser that let the duplicate through is unchanged (it lives in scraper/src, which this design session must not edit), so the next discovery cycle can re-mint the row - assert-repair-held.mjs own header records exactly that happening to T-277C merged duplicates. The held-proof (assert-repair-held.mjs with scripts/lib/repair-invariants/duplicate-ipo-rows.mjs, DUPLICATE_INVARIANT_FOLDS=assetreconstruction, --cycles 2) is RUNNING: the merge landed ~08:15 IST and discovery fires 08:30/11:00/14:00/17:30 IST, with the scraper waking every 30 min in between. NOTE ON TIMING - ipos.updated_at carries the known 5h30m skew, so it read 21:15Z for a merge that happened at 08:15 IST; do not derive wall-clock time from that column. Remaining for this finding: extend the normaliser to corporate-form words, run the duplicate check on discovery, then the held-proof.
findings.fix_in: data merge + normaliser fix + a duplicate detection check
findings.closed_in: Row merged on production 2026-09-09 ~08:15 IST and HELD across two real scraper cycles (last_scraped_at advanced twice; the duplicate did not return). Production duplicate count is 0 table-wide. The class fix - fold corporate-form words, run duplicate detection at discovery - is build item 12, and the detection that will catch the next one shipped with the repair: scripts/lib/repair-invariants/duplicate-ipo-rows.mjs.

findings.title: No rule exists for what happens when two rows converge on one identifier
findings.detail: Owner question 2026-09-09. Measured: NO open or upcoming IPO has an ISIN (0 of 19) - the depository assigns it near listing, so the only permanently unique id arrives AFTER the row is created and published. The duplicate second Asset Reconstruction row carries no identifier at all: no symbol, no ISIN, no CIN, no BSE number. So one-row-per-unique-id is right but unenforceable at insert. Design now carries late-binding identity: create on the normalised name, re-check every time a stronger identifier arrives, MERGE automatically on a converging symbol/CIN/ISIN keeping the union of fields and both provenances, and use CIN earlier (8 of 13 upcoming have it; it exists from incorporation, unlike a symbol or ISIN). The gap was never the identifiers - we hold four - it was having no rule for convergence. WORKED EXAMPLE 2026-09-09: the Asset Reconstruction merge (F-55) is the first time this convergence was resolved by hand, and scripts/merge-duplicate-ipo.mjs is what the rule would have to automate. What it settled in practice: the survivor is the row holding the strong identifiers (symbol/CIN/BSE number), never the one with the larger field count alone; a disagreeing strong identifier REFUSES the merge because it proves two offers; columns move only where the survivor is empty; person-created rows (watchlists, clicks, reviews, audit) are repointed while scraper-derived rows are deleted; the dropped slug becomes a redirect so the URL keeps resolving; and every moved column writes a field_sources row keeping previous_source. Those six decisions are the content the missing rule needs.
findings.closed_in: identity model written 2026-09-09

findings.trigger: the next time staging is used to prove anything about duplicate rows, or before any duplicate check is gated on staging
findings.title: Staging carries 12 duplicate IPO groups from a DIFFERENT defect: slug-suffix rows
findings.detail: Found 2026-09-09 while proving the duplicate invariant on both databases. Prod has ZERO duplicate groups; staging has 12, several with three or four rows: shree-balaji-mala-textiles-ltd has FOUR (plain, -ipo, -ipo-lt, -ipo-o), h-r-hygiene-products and g-v-electricals three each, plus gulf-lloyds -ct, laser-power-and-infra -o, indo-mim -o, silverstorm-parks -o, poojaa-precision -o, propshop-events -ct, caliber-mining -o, ic-electricals (co vs company), atharva-polyplast vs atharva-poly-plast. Every row inside a group carries an IDENTICAL issue_size, so this is not two sources disagreeing - it is one row minted repeatedly under suffixed slugs (-o, -lt, -ct, and slugs that embed the ipo name a second time). That is a slug-collision path, NOT the name-fold gap that produced the Asset Reconstruction duplicate (F-55), so fixing the normaliser will not clear them. Open dates are Jun-Jul 2026, so they are old rows, most likely repeated seeding. Why it matters: any duplicate check gated on staging goes permanently red at 12 violations, and staging stops being a usable proof surface for this class - which is precisely why scripts/lib/repair-invariants/duplicate-ipo-rows.mjs needed a DUPLICATE_INVARIANT_FOLDS scope to serve as a repair proof at all.
findings.fix_in: staging data clean-up, plus finding where the -o/-lt/-ct slug suffix is minted

findings.title: NSE returns an EMPTY issueInfo block for an SME IPO, so every SME-NSE rank that relies on an NSE LABEL is unproven
findings.detail: Probed 2026-09-09 against two live OPEN IPOs. /api/ipo-detail?symbol=ARCIL (mainboard) returns issueInfo.dataList with 39 labelled rows including Name of the Registrar, Book Running Lead Managers, Face Value, Tick Size, Bid Lot, Sponsor Bank, IPO Market Timings and Price Range. /api/ipo-detail?symbol=VINOD (SME, NSE Emerge) returns issueInfo as an EMPTY OBJECT - dataList length 0 - while still returning bidDetails and activeCat. /api/ipo-current-issue DOES carry the SME row (dates, series SME, symbol, noOfSharesOffered). So for SME on NSE the list row exists and the labelled issue-information block does not. Appendix A ranks NSE for SME_NSE on fields that only the labelled block carries. Evidence: probes/fixtures/nse/ipo-detail-ARCIL.json, probes/fixtures/nse/ipo-detail-VINOD.json, probes/fixtures/nse/ipo-current-issue.json.
findings.fix_in: Not fixed in this round on purpose: one observation of one live SME IPO is enough to FLAG a rank, not to re-rank a family of fields - that is the design's own standard of proof. Put to the review round with the saved payloads. If confirmed, the SME_NSE column needs a capability rule of its own and the ranks move to the document and Chittorgarh.

findings.title: Chittorgarh coverage differs per PAGE, and a per-page absence was recorded as a capability limit
findings.detail: The spec excluded peer_companies.pbv_ratio from Chittorgarh on one observation of one mainboard page on 2026-09-08. The Vinod Texworld page saved 2026-09-09 prints a company-level 'Price to Book Value 2.55 3.37' row and a peer table whose column header is 'P/BV Ratio'. The Asset Reconstruction page, three days into its issue, carries no peer table at all. So the source CAN serve the field and had simply not filled that page yet - which is NOT_AVAILABLE_YET on the plan row, not a missing capability.
findings.fix_in: field-source-resolution.spec.mjs: peer_companies.pbv_ratio removed from CG_CANNOT with the evidence cited inline. financial_data.pe_ratio stays excluded - the mainboard page's 'PE Ratio' column belongs to other recently listed IPOs, which is a different and still-live defect.

findings.title: F-46/F-55's stated root cause is wrong: the name normaliser already folds the corporate-form words
findings.detail: Verified live in Node against scraper/src/utils/company-name-normalizer.ts during the build-card round on 2026-09-09. 'ASSET RECONSTRUCTION COMPANY (INDIA) LIMITED' normalises to 'asset reconstruction company india' and 'Asset Reconstruction Co.(India) Ltd.' to 'asset reconstruction co india' - so the two still fail to collide, but NOT because company/co are missing from the suffix list. T-293 already added them. The real cause is pipeline ORDER: the parenthetical '(India)' is never made trailing before the company/co suffix regex runs, so the suffix is not in suffix position when the regex looks. The fix is a whole-word strip, matching the foldName already shipped in scripts/lib/repair-invariants/duplicate-ipo-rows.mjs - not adding words to a list that already contains them.
findings.fix_in: Build card item-12. The design section that names the fix as 'fold corporate-form words into the normaliser' must be corrected, or an implementer will add words that are already there, see no change, and conclude the finding was wrong.

findings.title: F-49 is narrower than 'valueActuallyChanged has no caller'
findings.detail: data-consolidation-service.ts:930 defines it and :932 uses it on the next line. It is a local const read exactly once, not a dead function. The real defect is the expression: valueChanged = !existingValueFromMap || (choseIncoming && (hadDifferentSource || valueActuallyChanged)) - the flag only decides the outcome when hadDifferentSource is false, and W-106's walk found that condition never held on any path it tested. A test that greps for callers would pass and prove nothing.
findings.fix_in: Build card item-15 replaces the caller test with a three-way counter split (writtenNoExisting / writtenDifferentSource / writtenSameSourceChanged) so the branch is observable.

findings.title: The ratios document is a ROUTING gap, not a zip gap - and this round's own brief got that wrong
findings.detail: The old-document-availability probe showed NSE serving offer documents as ZIP, and the build-card brief for item 8 concluded that unzipping was missing work. It is not: zip unwrapping already happens at download time (document-download-verifier.ts:307-325; document-store.ts always writes .pdf) and there is an NSE-ratios-specific override (isNseRatiosArchiveUrl, document-classifier.ts:181) that stops the bytes-win rule mislabelling the archive. The extract-real-pdf output shows the stored sha256 present and the document SKIPPED because the python filing extractor does not handle the type - a routing gap. Also found: financial_data.current_ratio, quick_ratio and inventory_turnover have no extraction or write-path code anywhere today, so they are genuinely new work rather than a wiring change.
findings.fix_in: Build card item-08 states the routing gap. Recorded here because the error was mine: a probe result read one step too literally became a brief that would have sent an implementer to build something that already exists.

findings.title: Section 5.2 presented all 37 amount columns as needing conversion; only 5 hold rupees today
findings.detail: The amount-columns probe classifies by MEANING (is this an aggregate rupee amount) and section 5.2 printed the result under the heading 'the columns that convert'. Read out of the writers on 2026-09-09: only ipos.issue_size, ipo_details.fresh_issue, ipo_details.ofs_issue, ipo_valuation.mcap_at_floor and ipo_valuation.mcap_at_cap hold rupees. financial_data.* and ipo_financials.* are already crore at the writer level (toCrore in financial-data-scraper.ts and the filing persister); anchor_investors.total_amount_raised is already crore; financial_statements.* never normalises by design and carries its own per-row unit. A repair tool built from the old table would have divided twenty-five already-crore columns by ten million.
findings.fix_in: The probe now records current_unit per CRORE column with the reason, and section 5.2 is regenerated from it with a 'unit stored TODAY' column and an explicit action per column.

findings.title: Build item 14 (BSE share count to rupees) is largely already built
findings.detail: computeBSEIssueSize (scraper/src/scrapers/bse-api-scraper.ts:147-151) already multiplies BSE's Issue_Size_No_of_shares by the floor price, and scraper/tests/unit/scrapers/bse-api-scraper.test.ts:113-130 carries three passing regression tests for it, referencing the earlier W-109/T-403 fixes. Section 7.1 lists item 14 as open work with a conversion test to write. Verified this session by reading both files.
findings.fix_in: Item 14's scope shrinks to: confirm the existing tests still assert the class, and confirm the two independent detection checks (c_issue_size_consistency, c_issue_size_floor, already recorded in docs/reviews/failure-classes/share-count-as-issue-size.json) run inside the pull model's nightly audit. Section 7.1's row must be corrected before an implementer rebuilds something that exists.

findings.title: The crore conversion silently activates a dormant scoring bug: every IPO currently scores as the largest possible
findings.detail: web/lib/services/ipo-scoring-realtime.ts:394-396 and web/lib/utils/rating-calculator.ts:164-168 compare issueSize against 1000/500/100 - crore-scale thresholds - while the column holds rupees. Asset Reconstruction's stored issue_size is 7,329,740,494, so it takes the top bucket, and so does every other IPO. Converting to crore makes the score discriminate for the first time, which is correct and is also a visible change to every IPO's rating on the day it ships.
findings.fix_in: Named in section 5.2 and owned by build item 11's release note. It is NOT fixed ahead of the conversion: changing the thresholds while the unit is still rupees would move every rating twice.

findings.title: Item 13's 'ofs_issue is never extracted' is stale for the share form
findings.detail: ipo_valuation.ofs_shares is already captured (filing-persister.ts:1297). What genuinely does not exist is USING it - cross-checking the share form against the rupee form - and the fresh + OFS = total within 0.5% write gate.
findings.fix_in: Build card item-13 states the narrower scope.

findings.title: The design undercounted the dead matrix keys by half, and mis-described what they are
findings.detail: Section 0.6 said '13 of the 77 matrix keys are dead duplicates in the wrong case'. Measured by probes/matrix-dead-keys.mjs on 2026-09-09: 27 of 77 are snake_case and therefore unreachable, because consolidation writes camelCase. Only 5 are duplicates (close_date, company_description, gmp_price, lot_size, open_date). The other 22 are ORPHANS - the live camelCase field has no matrix entry at all and silently takes DEFAULT_RULES every cycle, so its source order has never been chosen by anyone. They include total_subscription, retail_subscription, qib_subscription, nii_subscription, listing_price, issue_price, min_investment, roe_percentage, pb_ratio and peer_companies. The draft's own worked example was also wrong: revenue_fy1 is not a mis-cased revenueFy2022, it is the real camelCase name of a third table, ipo_financials (schema.ts:582-587), which nothing in scraper/src writes.
findings.fix_in: Section 0.6 is regenerated from the probe. Build item 3's scope grows: deleting 5 duplicates is cleanup; giving 22 orphaned live fields a chosen source order is the actual work.
